scope: Hays County Texas Paspalum langei herbarium vouchers, 2019/2021
source: University of Texas at Austin TEX Herbarium original sheet images indexed by GBIF; sheet media individually CC BY 4.0, institutional rights holder UT Austin
temporary_image_review: Run 43090970560, artifact 13888327539 (expires in one day); no image bytes committed into public repo
source_taxonomy: Paspalum langei accepted in Kew POWO and USDA GRIN, FNA describes species as perennial with 1–3(4) racemes, 2.1–3.3 mm paired imbricate spikelets, 0.4–1.2(1.8) mm lower glumes and papillose-based short hairs on upper glume/lower lemma.

actual_sheet_review.collector_metadata_discrepancy: 2021 sheet labels say Thomas L. Watson (2021-115, 2021-117), 2019 says Thomas J. Watson (2019-101); GBIF recordedBy incorrectly or differently lists Thomas J. Watson for all three. Do not assume two collectors or one collector until reconciled.
actual_sheet_review.habitat_provenance_uncertainty: 2019 residential yard could be planted; 2021 floodplain and shaded-slope plants have natural-habitat context. Neither alone is direct proof of wild establishment.

records.habitat_on_sheet: Partial shade on gradual slope in organic loam; associates include Carya illinoinensis, Quercus fusiformis, Rubus trivialis, Sorghum halepense, Wedelia hispida and Malvaviscus arboreus
records.landscape_context: Shaded roadside/upland slope; no planting reported
records.image_observed: Pressed basal foliage, leafy culms, several slender racemose branches with overlapping spikelets visible
records.limitations: First glume distribution and papilla-based hairs cannot be resolved at specimen sheet scan scale

records.habitat_on_sheet: Onion Creek floodplain, tire ruts collecting rainwater along primitive road, partial shade beneath Ulmus crassifolia, organic loam with Paspalum pubiflorum and Schizachyrium scoparium
records.landscape_context: Creekside conservation-area floodplain, not labeled planted
records.image_observed: Two rooted bunches of broad leaves and multiple narrow racemose flowering branches with paired-looking spikelets
records.limitations: Fine glume/sterile-lemma pubescence, lower glume lengths and comparison to sympatric Paspalum pubiflorum not resolved from scan

records.habitat_on_sheet: Residential yard in Goldenwood West subdivision, partial shade beneath Juniperus ashei
records.landscape_context: Residential yard; planted versus spontaneous unresolved
records.image_observed: Several narrow mature flowering racemes and broad leafy stems pressed across herbarium sheet
records.limitations: First glume, precise spikelet morphology and spontaneous occurrence cannot be proven from sheet/label

recommended_next: Request/find a TEX specimen annotation or high-res mature spikelet dissection showing lower glume and papillose pubescence, ideally TEX00568501 which co-occurred with P. pubiflorum; verify collection locality and taxon determiner before publishing a field ID card.
